title.value: Accelerating Neural Network Training: An Analysis of the Algo Perf Competition
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning and within the document.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025

A CCELERATING NEURAL NETWORK TRAINING : A N ANALYSIS OF THE A LGO P ERF COMPETITION

analysis.description: The paper discusses the Algo Perf competition, which focuses on speeding up the training of neural networks through improved training algorithms. It analyzes submissions from the competition, highlighting innovations in training speed through new algorithmic methods while controlling for hyperparameters. Key outcomes include insights on non-diagonal preconditioning and automated hyperparameter-free approaches.

type.justification: The paper involves empirical evaluation of neural network training algorithms using benchmarks and competition results.
type.quote: In the external tuning ruleset, submissions must provide workload-agnostic hyperparameter search spaces, while in the self-tuning ruleset they must be completely hyperparameter-free. In both rulesets, submissions are compared on time-to-result across multiple deep learning workloads, training on fixed hardware.

name.justification: The primary focus is on training algorithms and how they can be improved for faster training times.
name.quote: The goal of the A LGO P ERF : T RAINING A LGORITHMS competition is to evaluate practical speed-ups in neural network training achieved solely by improving the underlying training algorithms.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses empirical benchmarking through the Algo Perf competition to assess training algorithms.
name.quote: This competitive, time-to-result benchmark uses multiple realistic deep learning workloads on fixed hardware, allowing submitters to innovate solely on the training algorithms.

name.justification: A significant portion of the paper is dedicated to comparing hyperparameter-tuning strategies and their influence on training speed.
name.quote: In the external tuning ruleset, submissions must provide workload-agnostic hyperparameter search spaces, while in the self-tuning ruleset they must be completely hyperparameter-free.

name.justification: The model was a winning submission in the competition and effectively utilized non-diagonal preconditioning.
name.quote: The winning submission in the external tuning ruleset, using D ISTRIBUTED S HAMPOO , demonstrates the effectiveness of non-diagonal preconditioning over popular methods like A DAM.

is_contributed.justification: The paper contributes by effectively showcasing the model's performance in a competitive setting.
